request.description: Train a fresh PPO baseline with the current policy, reward, and 0.14-0.20 m training-radius recipe.
request.rationale: No candidate or behavioral evidence exists yet. This full-ceiling baseline establishes whether the current recipe can learn stable uninterrupted holds on its training support and produces the first candidate for diagnostics on the official 0.06-0.20 m geometry. That separates basic optimization or stabilization failure from the unresolved inner-radius generalization and branch-robustness explanations before changing the scientific method.

request.description: Evaluate the peak-training-success and terminal T1 candidates on the shared 160-episode official-distribution research panel, retaining per-episode target geometry and reach-and-hold diagnostics.
request.rationale: T1 training success reaches 0.97 at checkpoint-100352 and remains 0.95 at checkpoint-120832, establishing that the current torque policy and reward can learn holds on the 0.14-0.20 m training support but not whether this transfers to the official 0.06-0.20 m distribution. A paired panel distinguishes checkpoint selection effects from systematic geometry or stabilization failure; radius-stratified first-entry, maximum hold, interruptions, and distance diagnostics test whether failures concentrate in the unseen inner band or arise across the support.

request.cumulative_resource_use: One fresh training run requested at 120000 steps, completing 120832 simulator steps through rollout rounding, and one paired research evaluation of two T1 candidates over 160 shared episode seeds. request.current_goal_gap: The best measured candidates are 94.375% on the 160-episode official-distribution research panel, 3.625 percentage points below the 98% target, and neither candidate has been shown on the protected 200-episode assessment. The nine observed failures are not explained by radius coverage alone: they occur across the full 0.06-0.20 m radius range and cluster in a negative target-angle sector.
request.current_synthesis: Established observations: T1 reached 0.97 training success at checkpoint-100352 and 0.95 at checkpoint-120832 on the 0.14-0.20 m training distribution. M1 evaluated both on the same 160 official-distribution seeds; each achieved 151/160 (94.375%), with zero discordant outcomes. In the checkpoint-100352 diagnostics, all nine failures were at target angles from -150.6 to -118.8 degrees, while target radii ranged from 0.077 to 0.188 m; six failures never entered tolerance and three reached it only briefly (maximum holds of 1-2 steps). The terminal candidate shows the same failing seeds and the same angular concentration. Interpretation: the common, angle-localized failure is more consistent with an asymmetric branch-selection or angular-coverage mechanism than with a generic inability to stabilize or a purely inner-radius generalization gap. The physical model predicts that elbow branch choice, initial-singularity escape, shoulder-limit margins, and stopping margin can make angular sectors behaviorally distinct. Competing explanations remain: (a) the policy has learned a brittle branch or asymmetric route in that sector, (b) the observation/reward and training distribution create a representation or sampling weakness around the wrapped angular branch transition, or (c) the apparent sector is a finite-panel artifact masking a broader dynamic stopping problem. M1 cannot identify the selected branch, joint-limit margins, endpoint velocity, or control saturation, and the 160-episode result is not an official assessment.
request.decision_frontier: Does the localized negative-angle failure arise from branch selection and angular policy coverage, or from a dynamics/stabilization limitation that merely appears angular? Discriminating evidence is a targeted diagnostic measurement that records branch identity or IK-branch proximity, joint-limit and Jacobian margins, endpoint/joint velocity, action saturation, entry timing, and hold interruptions across the failing sector and matched successful angles/radii. A branch/coverage result would justify changing target/angle coverage or branch-aware policy learning; a velocity/settling result would instead justify redesigning stabilization or reward dynamics.
request.human_goal_connection: The human objective requires at least 196 complete 100-step holds in the 200-episode official assessment. T1 demonstrates that the current PPO recipe can learn the reach-and-hold behavior on its restricted training support, but M1 measures only 151 of 160 successes on the official geometry and therefore leaves a material, localized gap to 98%.
request.next_direction_or_closure: End startup and enter goal review with a bounded inquiry on the angular failure mechanism. The first inquiry action should be a targeted, reusable diagnostic measurement of the shared failing seeds and matched angular controls, extending the existing evaluation evidence with branch, conditioning, velocity, saturation, and hold-timing observables before selecting a training or policy intervention.

request.description: Run a targeted I1 diagnostic on T1:checkpoint-100352: replay the shared 160-episode research panel and evaluate a matched 40-case grid at radii 0.07, 0.11, 0.15, and 0.19 m over failing angles -151 to -119 degrees and adjacent control angles -115 to -83 degrees. Record per-control-step branch proximity and identity, joint-limit and Jacobian margins, endpoint and joint velocity, action saturation, entry and low-velocity timing, and uninterrupted-hold interruptions.
request.rationale: M1 established a repeated failure sector but measured only distance and hold counts. This measurement directly contrasts the failing sector with matched-radius adjacent controls while replaying the original panel, so branch/coverage evidence can be separated from angularly exposed velocity, saturation, settling, or hold-interruption dynamics before allocating the next 120000-step intervention.

request.outcome: I1 is resolved in favor of an angular and geometry-coverage mechanism with joint-limit exposure, rather than a primary branch-identity or generic stabilization failure. The matched diagnostic used the elbow-positive branch at entry and terminal state in every case, with no observed branch switching. The failing sector achieved 15/20 successes versus 20/20 in matched adjacent controls. Failing-sector entries had a mean minimum joint-limit margin of about 0.12 rad versus 0.49 rad for controls, and somewhat higher endpoint and joint speeds, while Jacobian conditioning and action saturation were comparable. The next intervention should therefore expand target support to the official radius range and improve sampling of the exposed negative-angle sector; it should not first redesign generic hold stabilization.
request.reason: M2 directly measured the closure variables on the 160-episode replay and a matched 40-case grid. The evidence supports angular/geometry coverage and limit-margin exposure as the goal-linked mechanism: branch identity is invariant across groups, conditioning is not materially worse in the failing sector, and high saturation is common to both failures and successful controls. The measurement does not prove that velocity is irrelevant, because failing entries are faster and the low-velocity criterion was never reached, but it makes velocity a coupled secondary risk rather than the primary discriminator. M2 therefore justifies a full-distribution and failing-sector coverage intervention before any stabilization-specific redesign.
